item.title: How the Foo Fighters Fill a Three-Hour Set List, Night After Night

item.title: Tupac Shakur Murder Trial: Takeaways From Week 2

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Marriage to Carl Dean Was Fueled by Distance and Difference
item.description: Dolly Parton met Carl Dean outside a Nashville laundromat in 1964. For decades, she was as protective of her marriage as he was fiercely private.
item.dc:creator: Derrick Bryson Taylor

item.title: Olivia Rodrigo, Prince: Songs to Know This Week

item.dc:creator: Jon Pareles

item.title: ‘Les Misérables’ Review: The Barricades Rise Above the Hudson
item.description: In this semi-open-air staging in the Hudson Valley, the musical conjures Paris’s seedy cobblestone streets with an adept Jean Valjean leading the charge.
item.dc:creator: Helen Shaw
item.media:description: “Les Misérables,” performed by Hudson Valley Shakespeare’s 21-person company in Garrison, N.Y.

item.title: Floating Points Makes Music for the Dance Floor, and Ballet

item.dc:creator: Hugh Morris and Michael Vince Kim
item.media:description: Floating Points, the D.J. and composer whose real name is Sam Shepherd.

item.title: A New Documentary Gives Butthole Surfers Their Due
item.description: A new movie explores Butthole Surfers’ musical legacy, with layers of loss and regret. “It’s kind of vindicating,” the singer Gibby Haynes said.
item.dc:creator: Mark Yarm

item.title: Judge Says Trump’s Name Should Stay Off Kennedy Center for Now
item.description: After the court forced the removal of the president’s name from the building’s title, the center devised a plan to add an inscription honoring President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague and Julia Jacobs
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:description: Though President Trump’s name was taken down weeks ago, the scaffolding and tarps used in the process remain up outside the Kennedy Center.

item.title: Governor Bill Lee Joins Push to Rename Nashville Airport for Dolly Parton
item.description: Gov. Bill Lee of Tennessee and other officials are moving to overcome bureaucracy and politics to put the beloved superstar’s name on Nashville International Airport.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung and Emily Cochrane
item.media:description: “Who doesn’t want to be ‘departin’ from Parton’?” said one of the fans behind an online petition to rename Nashville International Airport for Dolly Parton, who died on Tuesday.

item.title: Jaye P. Morgan, Hit-Making Singer and Bawdy TV Personality, Dies at 94
item.description: With a humorous stage name adapted from that of the New York financier, she made a 1950s Hit Parade splash and later was a flamboyant talk-show regular.
item.dc:creator: Joanne Kaufman
item.media:credit: CBS Photo Archive, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Jaye P. Morgan in 1954 with different models of CBS microphones. The next year, she scored a batch of hits like “That’s All I Want From You” and “Danger! Heartbreak Ahead.”

item.title: Why Andy Warhol Couldn’t Capture Dolly Parton
item.description: Andy Warhol’s images of Parton don’t strike me as up to the level of his best society portraits; they aren’t quite worthy of the singer’s complex excellence.
item.dc:creator: Blake Gopnik

item.title: Harry Styles Kicks Off Monthslong Residency at Madison Square Garden
item.description: The singer kicked off a monthslong residency at the venue on Wednesday night before a giddy crowd.
item.dc:creator: Leah Greenblatt
item.media:description: Harry Styles’s public demeanor is consistently sincere and sunny, impish but affirming.

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Cautious Politics Resulted in Widespread Affection

item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs
item.media:description: Dolly Parton, whose death was announced on Tuesday, kept partisan politics at a distance throughout her career.

item.title: Harry Styles Fans Camp Out for the Best View of the Star
item.description: As early as Tuesday, general admission ticket holders waited for the line (before the line) that would determine their vantage points at Wednesday night’s show.
item.dc:creator: Malia Mendez
item.media:description: Derek Alderton, from the United Kingdom, was among the Harry Styles fans outside Madison Square Garden hours before the concert.

item.title: Janie Bradford, Co-Writer of Motown’s First Hit, Dies at 87
item.description: One of the label’s first hires, she worked on “Money (That’s What I Want)” and went on to have a hand in many other songs.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:credit: ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Janie Bradford, center, with members of the Oak Ridge Boys in 1974. During the early years of Motown, she worked the front desk and handled contracts along with writing songs.

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library Changes Lives. Some States Gut It Anyway.
item.description: The crown jewel of the singer’s philanthropic efforts has handed out hundreds of millions of books to children over the past 31 years. But it isn’t immune to funding cuts.
item.dc:creator: Ash Wu
item.media:description: A cardboard cutout of Dolly Parton greets attendees at the 2025 National Book Festival in Washington, D.C.

item.title: How Dollywood Captured the Essence of Dolly Parton

item.dc:creator: Melena Ryzik
item.media:credit: John Seakwood/Disney General Entertainment Content, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Dolly Parton riding the Dollywood Express in 1987. Her namesake theme park grew into one of the most popular tourist attractions in the South.

item.title: Why Dolly Parton Wouldn’t Let Elvis Presley Record ‘I Will Always Love You’

item.title: Dolly Parton Was a Trailblazer in Business, Too

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Viral Moments, From the Grammys With Whitney Houston to Her Moderna Vaccine Song

item.dc:creator: Claire Moses

item.media:description: Dolly Parton in 1976.

item.title: Harry Styles and the Residencies Taking Over the Music Industry

item.title: Dolly Parton Died After Brief Period With Cancer

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Death Hits Home for Tennesseans: ‘She Was One of Us’
item.description: The country music star kept her home state at the forefront of her music and work. “She inspired Tennesseans to be better,” one resident said.

item.title: Dolly Parton: A Life in Pictures

item.title: Dolly Parton Was Someone We Could All Agree On. Even in Polls.

item.title: Dolly Parton Wanted to Share Her Story on Broadway. She Still Will.

item.title: Dolly Parton, Country Music Superstar Whose Songs Spoke to Millions, Dies at 80

item.title: Trump Lawyers Warn That Kennedy Center Might Need Demolition if Not Fixed

item.media:description: Lawyers for the Trump administration said in a court filing that if the Kennedy Center does not undergo planned renovations, it could be replaced by a large amphitheater overlooking the Potomac River.
